name: Gaussian Texture Filtering via Jacobian Back-projection
definition: A technique to compute the color of a screen pixel by integrating the texture signal against a Gaussian filter, where the filter is back-projected from screen space to texture space using the local affine approximation (Jacobian) of the texture mapping.
summary: Gaussian Texture Filtering via Jacobian Back-projection reduces aliasing by adapting a Gaussian filter to surface distortion using the Jacobian matrix, unlike methods relying on pre-filtered mipmaps.
